result.note: Official industrial output data for August 2026; tested the headline growth figure and its composition by use-based category.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's industrial output data for August 2026, released in September 2026:
items: Capital goods led the growth, rising 16.9%.
Consumer non-durables grew more slowly than overall industrial output.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Overall output rose 8%, capital goods led at 16.9%, and consumer non-durables managed just 2.1%, well below the headline figure. The gap suggests the investment-led boom is not yet reaching ordinary households.
questions.source: India's industrial output grew 8% in August, led by capital goods at 16.9%, though everyday consumer non-durables rose just 2.1%, a sign the boom is not yet reaching ordinary households.
